sections.h2: What is Goodhue County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Goodhue County sits in southeastern Minnesota on the Wisconsin border, across Lake Pepin, with Red Wing as the county seat. The legislature carved it out of Wabasha County on March 5, 1853, and it was named for James Madison Goodhue, who published the first newspaper in the territory. Wheat built the early economy, and for several years the county led the country in wheat output. Today the ground is rolling hills and bluffs cut by the Cannon River, and traffic runs on U.S. 52, 61 and 63.

Census QuickFacts gives a picture of the housing a seller is dealing with:

  • 48,195 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 1.3% since the 2020 census.
  • 19,727 households, with 78.8% of homes lived in by their owners.
  • A median owner-occupied home value of $285,100 and a median household income of $84,171.
  • 84 building permits in 2025 across 21,445 housing units.

Cities include Red Wing, Cannon Falls, Zumbrota, Kenyon, Wanamingo, Goodhue and pieces of Lake City and Pine Island. Red Wing Public Schools, Cannon Falls, Zumbrota-Mazeppa and Kenyon-Wanamingo are among the school districts that levy on county homes.

sections.h2: Which Goodhue County office handles property tax?
sections.html:
Finance and Taxpayer Services runs both the assessor and the auditor/treasurer from the second floor of the Government Center, 509 W. 5th St. in Red Wing. The phone is 651-385-3040 and the counter is open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. For assessor questions, choose option 1.

The county reminds owners that its board controls only the county budget and levy. Of thirteen reasons a bill can move, which include a change in your value, a shift in other owners' values, city or township levies, school levies, referendums, special assessments and state aid or law changes, only the county piece belongs to the commissioners. A seller who sees a jump should check which piece moved before calling.

sections.h2: When are Goodhue County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Minnesota Statutes 279.01 splits the bill into two halves, payable before May 16 and before October 16 when the tax on a parcel is over $100. Agricultural homestead and qualifying farm land may pay the second half without penalty through November 15.

Penalty starts at 2 percent on homestead and 4 percent on nonhomestead on the day after a due date. It is repeated on the first of the next month, then 1 percent monthly through December, topping out at 8 percent for homestead and 12 percent for nonhomestead. The treasurer must abate a late penalty once if the envelope was postmarked within one business day of the due date and the owner has not used that abatement before.

Owners can search records and pay from the Finance page link labeled Search Property Tax Records/Pay Property Tax, and the office can quote a payoff for a parcel before closing.

sections.h2: How does Goodhue County arrive at my value?
sections.html:
The assessor estimates market value and classification for more than 29,000 parcels as of January 2, and the figure sets taxes payable the following year. Staff try to view the inside and outside of each home, list size, age, quality, basement finish and extras, and feed that into a mass appraisal system that a county appraiser reviews. Sales from October 1 through September 30 before the assessment date are the guide.

State rules require every property to be physically reviewed at least once every five years and require the overall level of assessment to land between 90 and 105 percent of market value. The county says it consistently meets that test. Classification matters as much as value: homestead, nonhomestead residential, apartment and commercial are each taxed at a percentage set by the legislature. The county is also doing on-site reassessments in several areas during 2026, so a seller whose neighborhood is on that list should expect a visit request.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Goodhue County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with facts. Pull recent sales of comparable homes and any market analysis, then call the assessor at 651-385-3040 option 1 and walk an appraiser through them. An interior inspection can be scheduled. If the question is still open, go to the local board of appeal and equalization, then make an appointment with the county board. The county board listing shows a June 15 meeting by appointment only, and the call to book it goes through the same number.

Goodhue County appeal path, from the county assessor's appeal page
StepWhereDetail
1AssessorGather sales, call 651-385-3040 option 1, review with an appraiser
2Interior inspectionSchedule if the appraiser asks
3Local boardAttend the meeting for your city or township
4County boardAppointment only, 509 W. 5th St., Red Wing
5Minnesota Tax CourtPhone 651-539-3260; filing deadline April 30

Only the current year valuation can go through the boards. The county says an appeal of a prior year value runs through Tax Court alone, and Statutes 278.01 sets April 30 of the tax year as the court filing date.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when I sell a Goodhue County house?
sections.html:
Delinquent tax comes first. Under Minnesota Statutes 272.12 the auditor checks a deed for delinquent tax before transfer, and the recorder will not file it without the auditor's note. If the sale covers only part of a parcel, Statutes 272.121 calls for the treasurer's certification that the full-parcel tax for the current year is paid.

For an ordinary whole-parcel sale, ask the title company how this year's first and second halves will be split, and ask Finance and Taxpayer Services for the amount still open on the parcel. Buyers who plan to live in the home should apply for homestead; the county assessor's notice says people who bought or moved into a property in the past year may qualify for a property tax refund.

faqs.q: Who sets property values in Goodhue County?
faqs.a: The county assessor, working from the Government Center in Red Wing. Values are set as of January 2 and mailed to owners in March. Call 651-385-3040 option 1 with questions.

faqs.q: When is the Goodhue County board of appeal and equalization?
faqs.a: The county page lists June 15, by appointment only. Call 651-385-3040 option 1 to book a time before then, after trying the local board for your city or township.

faqs.q: Can I appeal last year's Goodhue County value?
faqs.a: Only through Minnesota Tax Court. The county says prior year values cannot go to its boards, and the court filing must be made by April 30 of the year the taxes are due.

faqs.q: What are the Goodhue County tax due dates?
faqs.a: Half is due before May 16 and half before October 16, per Minnesota Statutes 279.01. Qualifying agricultural property can pay the second half by November 15 without penalty.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay delinquent tax to sell my Goodhue County home?
faqs.a: Yes. A deed cannot be recorded until the auditor certifies no delinquent tax remains, so the payoff is normally handled at closing by the title company.
